If you’re looking for a stable, reliable way to make money, then credit card processing may be right for you. With an average yearly salary of just over $49,000 according to Glassdoor, credit card processing agents can build a career while doing interesting work. 

Becoming a credit card processing agent can be a lucrative opportunity, but it’s important to understand the process and what’s involved before diving in. 

In this article, we’ll outline the steps you need to take to become a credit card processing agent and provide some tips on how to get started.

Want to become a credit card processing agent at an industry leading provider?

Contact Us

Getting started as a credit card processing agent

There are a few key things you will need to know before diving into the world of credit card processing and merchant account sales. So, what exactly does it entail?

A credit card processing agent, also called a payment processing agent or merchant account agent, works with an independent sales organization (ISO) or merchant services provider (MSP) to provide businesses with payment processes that suit their needs. With an understanding of the payment industry and merchant needs, you can help businesses increase their bottom line.

Here’s what you’ll need to know to get started:

  • Basic understanding of payment processing: You don’t need to be an expert to get started. You don’t even necessarily need to have a sales background. However, you will need to learn the fundamentals of the industry and how to match products and services to merchant needs. You should be familiar with credit and merchant credit card processing and the rates and fees associated with credit card transactions as well as risk management. Consider taking courses on credit card transactions or fraud prevention techniques. Be sure to familiarize yourself with concepts like chargebacks, payment processing, and payment gateways vs. merchant accounts.
  • Pick a niche: The credit card processing industry is fragmented and competitive. Because of this, it’s best to become an expert in a particular area or market segment, such as restaurants, hotels, or high-risk merchants. After you’ve learned a little bit about the ins and outs of payment processing, do a little digging to find a niche market that you’d like to specialize in. By focusing on one area that matches your interests and values, you will be able to understand the unique needs of your target market while also holding knowledge about the payment industry as a whole. This powerful combination will allow you to build trust and build a solid network.
  • Apply to your ISO or MSP of choice: Do some research on reputable ISO and MSP programs and compare them to find which ones are right for you. Apply and wait for approval. Although credit card processing agents often work as independent contractors, some ISOs and MSPs may require you to be an employee. In this case, you will be reimbursed for any expenses incurred. When looking into programs, ask yourself, do they have experience in your chosen niche? What is their professional reputation? Do their mission and values align with your own? You might even reach out to current credit card agents within those programs to get more insight and find out which one is right for you.

💡 Pro-tip: TailoredPay is looking for credit card processing agents. If you’d like to partner with a brand merchants across the United States trust, contact sales@tailoredpay.com.

  • Get the word out: Once you’ve done your research, found your niche, and joined an ISO/MSP, it’s time to get your name out there. Create a website and social media accounts to promote your services. Distribute business cards, pamphlets, and flyers. Use social media to your advantage. Contests, giveaways, and other promotions are a great way to get credit card processing agents in the door so you can start selling credit card processing.
  • Start selling: Even if you’ve done your research and found the credit card processing program that’s right for you, actually selling credit card processing can be quite difficult. Don’t give up. Successful credit card processing agents often experience a lot of rejection and disappointment before they find the right credit card processors for their merchant clients. Get out there and make connections. Build a network of professionalism and trust and you’ll be well on your way to success as a credit card processing agent!

Tips for success as a credit card processing agent

Keep these tips in mind when starting your credit card processing business:

  • Be professional: Be responsible. Promote honesty and integrity throughout the credit card process. When you’re asking someone to trust you with their most sensitive financial information, it’s important that they know they can rely on you.
  • Be a consistent learner: The credit card industry is in a constant state of change, and it can be difficult to keep up with all the new credit card news. It’s important to stay informed if you want your credit card processing business to succeed.
  • Be persistent: Working in credit card processing requires meeting deadlines, dealing with regulations, handling sensitive information, and much more. Don’t let challenges get in the way of success; keep pushing forward.
  • Make connections: When credit card processing agents make deals with merchants, it’s important to build trust and establish relationships. Make sure they understand your credit card processing services and they know what you have to offer. As you build up your credit card processing business, be sure to maintain strong, positive relationships with your clients.
